title: UDLM Conformance Declaration
description: The declaration an implementation publishes at /.well-known/udlm/conformance (CONFORMANCE.md §4). WIR-035 requires a declaration to match this schema. Transcribed from §4.1's example and §4.2's field-semantics table, which agree on all thirteen top-level fields. Where the two documents state nothing — the shape of the nested objects, and which interop surfaces exist — this schema deliberately does NOT invent a constraint. Those are recorded as open in the issue that produced it, because a schema that guesses becomes the requirement.

record_type.description: Top-level dispatch discriminator (data-model-core §2). Not part of the published declaration body §4.1 shows — it is how a record in this registry is routed to this schema, the same way every other record kind is.

implementation.description: Self-identification. The three members are those §4.1 shows; §4.2 describes the field only as a whole, so they are required on the example's authority and nothing further is asserted about them.

udlm_version.description: The udlm semver this implementation conforms to.

profile.description: The active profile, by handle. Not a closed list: the six standard postures (homelab, dev, standard, prod, fsi, sovereign) are the UDLM Profile Set's, and an organization authors its own in its own namespace (`acme/profile/regulated-eu`, never `udlm/`). A profile is a record (profile.schema.json); this field names which one is active.

exclusions.description: Contract names not implemented. Required when level is partial (see allOf); a full declaration may still carry it empty, which §4.1's example does.

schema_bundle_url.description: Where to fetch the schema bundle. Not typed as a URI: §4.1 shows a root-relative path (/.well-known/udlm/schema-bundle), which format:uri-reference admits and format:uri does not.

interop_surfaces.description: Which surfaces are available and how to reach them. The surface NAMES are deliberately not enumerated: consumer_api, provider_callbacks, federation and audit_export appear only as keys in §4.1's example and are defined as a set nowhere in the spec. An enum here would invent the vocabulary rather than record it. Each entry's shape is constrained because §4.1 is consistent about it.

leap_second_strategy.description: The peer's declared leap-handling strategy. Deliberately unconstrained — time-and-clock.md §8 states an implementation MAY use ANY strategy preserving audit traceability, naming smearing and leap-aware representation as examples rather than as a vocabulary, and §4.2 calls it a 'named, open set'. An enum here would close a set the contract holds open on purpose.

auth_mechanism_for_schema_endpoints.description: How peers authenticate to fetch schemas.

conformance_test_suite_version.description: Which version of the conformance test suite was run (§8). Note that the suite does not yet exist — #417 — so this field cannot be populated honestly today; it is required here because §4.2 requires it, and softening that would hide the gap rather than close it.

self_certified_at.description: RFC 3339 UTC instant when self-certification was performed.

independent_verification.description: Present only if independently verified (§8). Members are those §4.1 shows; §4.2 describes the field only as a whole, so none is asserted required.

then.description: §4.2: exclusions is required when level is partial. A partial claim that does not say what is excluded is not a partial claim — it is a full claim with the difficult part left out.
